summary: Revision 1 correctly prohibits real SDK execution and supports a bounded local preflight, but the canary design does not yet guarantee its declared safe failure scope or establish all advertised controls. Revise the network probe, required operation/evidence matrix, pre-execution review order, and NO-RUN completion branch before implementation/execution proceeds. This review does not approve any real host execution.

open_findings.title: The reserved-IP negative probe can emit external traffic when the control under test fails
open_findings.impact: A documentation address is not an independently enforced local-only destination. Attempting a connection can send packets through the host network stack if the sandbox is absent, misconfigured, or bypassed. Therefore the test's failure branch violates the stated no-external-request scope before it can report NO-RUN. A refusal, timeout, or unreachable error also does not establish sandbox denial.
open_findings.required_correction: Remove routed destination attempts from this preflight. Use only demonstrably local synthetic socket operations with no application payload and an explicit safe unexpected-success cleanup path, and narrow the reported evidence to those operations. If general egress denial requires a separate independently established containment mechanism that is unavailable here, mark that control unverified and the future host NO-RUN. Do not infer external egress enforcement from documentation-address routing failure.

open_findings.title: Four unnamed negative canaries are insufficiently specified for the advertised boundary
open_findings.impact: The plan claims denied filesystem reads and writes, socket/listener absence, and child execution, but it does not require separate attributable checks for these operations. A single filesystem failure cannot prove both read and write controls; a connection failure cannot prove bind/listen denial; and a spawn failure cannot by itself demonstrate the intended fork/exec distinction. Missing files, ordinary permissions, unused ports, and an invalid child executable could yield false positives. Unexpected successful child/socket operations have no specified safe ownership/termination design.
open_findings.required_correction: Specify a bounded required-operation matrix before implementation: independently accessible synthetic denied-read and denied-write targets outside the child's allowed roots but inside the parent's owned fixture; allowed input read and scratch write; each socket operation/family actually claimed, including listener creation if that claim remains; and a valid harmless exact-runtime child attempt. Require attributable sandbox-denial outcomes rather than generic failure and separate launcher-startup permission from subsequent child-creation denial. Define independently bounded cleanup for unexpected child/socket success and timeout/output exhaustion. Narrow unsupported claims and return NO-RUN for any control needed by the future host that cannot be exercised safely.

open_findings.title: The completion rule excludes the intended unsupported-platform NO-RUN outcome
open_findings.impact: Missing sandbox support, a denied positive control, or a failed negative control must produce NO-RUN, yet completion requires isolation-canaries to pass and every denial criterion to be satisfied. This conflates successful investigation with successful containment and leaves the valid unsupported-control outcome unable to complete honestly.
open_findings.required_correction: Define two terminal branches. READY_FOR_REVIEW requires every required positive/negative containment control to pass. NO-RUN may complete the bounded investigation with the actual unavailable/failed/unverified controls recorded, successful containment criteria left unsatisfied, cleanup outcome recorded, and the real-host dependency held. Define report fields and check/exit semantics so the ledger never records a failed containment check as passed merely because the harness reported NO-RUN correctly; keep unresolved cleanup failure explicitly unresolved.

open_findings.title: Independent review is not explicitly ordered before the first canary execution
open_findings.impact: The canary runner performs unsandboxed fixture creation/cleanup and launches operations whose policy may fail. The current independent code gate could occur only after actual execution because it is tied to source/evidence hashes. That would leave the first execution's exact profile, destinations, cleanup scope, and limits unreviewed.
open_findings.required_correction: Require an independent static code/security review of the concrete runner, profile, canary bodies, exact runtime invocation, and failure-effect manifest before the first canary execution. Then run only those reviewed hashes and perform a separate review of resulting evidence. This is a sequencing gate within already authorized local work, not a request for new user approval.

observations: Read only the assigned role, matching skill, plan revision 1, contract, static research report, and planner handoff packet. No repository implementation, runtime SDK, user configuration, secret, or network was accessed.

The plan and contract SHA-256 values were independently confirmed with shasum and match the reviewed binding. The source_sha256 is preserved from the coordinator-supplied binding; the underlying source digest was not independently recomputed within this artifact-only assignment.

The provided planner packet is an assignment rather than the planner's final proposal. The coordinator's assignment separately attests that the delivered planner result recommends NO-RUN for the real SDK; this review does not claim to have inspected that result.

The SDK-free restriction, preservation of the broader build-delivery SSOT, exact-hash re-review expectation, clean child environment intent, and prohibition on treating application-level fetch controls as OS containment are appropriate.
Existing local implementation authorization is sufficient for preparation after plan corrections. No repeated user approval is requested by this review.

Unavailable or unsupported enforcement, ambiguous denials, and incomplete evidence must remain NO-RUN for the future SDK. Even a successful corrected preflight provides only evidence for the tested operations and cannot authorize or certify real host execution.

The plan identifies revision, owners, scope, and dependencies. Add an explicit initial-revision change-history entry and identify the concrete planner-result artifact in the next revision for traceability; these are optional documentation improvements rather than separate blocking findings.
